title: Salih and the she-camel
hook: Thamud are given a she-camel as a sign and told to let her graze (7:73–79)

segments.voice: Yesterday: Hud and 'Ad, and the wind. Your line was towers aren't safety. What did you notice yourself building? Today, the next people in surah seven, and the next brother sent to them. Day four hundred ten.

In northwest Arabia, near the town of al-Ula, enormous tombs are carved straight into sandstone cliffs, their doorways cut like temple fronts. Muslim tradition has long linked this region, al-Hijr, with the people of Thamud. Archaeologists date the carved tombs standing there now to the Nabataeans, a later people. But the Qur'an says Thamud, too, carved homes out of mountains. And it tells of a sign sent to them that wasn't a wall or a tower at all. It was an animal. A she-camel.
screen: `TOMBS CARVED INTO CLIFFS.` → `AL-HIJR, AND THAMUD.` → `A SIGN THAT WAS AN ANIMAL.`

segments.voice: Verse seventy-three: to Thamud, their brother Salih. Same message as Hud: worship Allah, you have no god but Him. Then he points to a sign. This is the she-camel of Allah, a sign for you. Let her eat in Allah's earth, and don't touch her with harm, or a painful punishment will take you. The Arabic is naqat Allah, the camel of God, and the phrase gives an ordinary animal enormous dignity. Surah twenty-six adds a detail: the water was to be shared, a day for her to drink and a day for the people. The test was almost too simple. Leave her alone. Share the well. That's all. Salih reminds them of their blessings: Allah made them successors after 'Ad, gave them plains to build palaces on and mountains to carve into homes. The proud chiefs mock the poorer people who believed. And then, verse seventy-seven, they hamstring the she-camel and say to Salih, bring on what you threaten. Surah ninety-one says it was done by the most wretched of them, while the people went along. The earthquake took them, and morning found them fallen in their homes. When the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ later passed through al-Hijr on the way to Tabuk, Bukhari reports that he told his companions not to enter the dwellings of those who were punished except in tears. Elsewhere, hadith tell of a man forgiven for giving water to a thirsty dog, and a woman punished for starving a cat. In this tradition, how people treat an animal is never a small thing.
screen: `THEIR BROTHER SALIH.` · `NAQAT ALLAH — THE CAMEL OF GOD.` · `A DAY TO DRINK, A DAY FOR YOU.` · `THEY HAMSTRUNG HER.` · then, large: `LEAVE HER TO GRAZE.`

segments.voice: Sit, and breathe. Picture an animal you'll likely cross today: a pigeon on the sidewalk, a neighbor's dog, a cat in an alley, a bee at a window. See it going about its business, eating, drinking, resting. Then picture yourself simply letting it be: not chasing, not shooing, not honking, not swatting. Maybe leaving a little water out. Hold that picture of an animal left in peace. The bell holds the time.
Salih. A prophet sent to Thamud, and a sign, a she-camel, that asked only to be left in peace and given her share of water. Today's word.
Your line: leave her to graze. Today, leave one animal in peace, on purpose, and if you can, set out some water. Day four hundred ten.

howItsDone: Muslims honor Salih as a prophet sent to Thamud; his story is taught alongside hadith on kindness to animals, and teachers recall the reports about the Prophet passing al-Hijr.

fork.setup: you're one of Thamud. the she-camel drinks from your well on her day. what does Salih ask?
options: leave her and share the water, a day each.
fork.reveal: let her eat in Allah's earth and touch her not with harm. they hamstrung her instead, and the earthquake came.

original.note: Arabic: a she-camel. naqat Allah: the she-camel of God (7:73).

trapdoor: what you thought: a miracle camel.
what it means: a sign that asked almost nothing, leave her be, share the water, and a people who couldn't do it.
what a scholar hears: 7:77 uses 'aqaru, they hamstrung; 91:12 and 54:29 single out one man who did it while the people consented, so commentators hold the whole people responsible.

sources.ref: Sahih al-Bukhari 2363 (the dog given water); Sahih al-Bukhari 3318 (the cat)

notes: Al-Hijr / Mada'in Salih near al-Ula: the visible tombs are Nabataean (roughly 1st century BCE–1st century CE); tradition links the region with Thamud. Confirm phrasing.
Hadith numbers (Bukhari 433, 2363, 3318) cited from memory; confirm.
Collective responsibility reading of 91:12 / 54:29 summarized from tafsir; confirm.

Editor review (2026-10-01): first naming is now 'the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ'; howItsDone no longer claims 'many pilgrims' know the reports. Bukhari 433 does not itself name Tabuk (Bukhari 4419 does); confirm.
